conclusions.text: The ten complete issue components each have positive source-union intersection and a nonempty residual outside the consumed source union. The bounded local country-union comparison also finds source-covered portions outside the current local Atlas ADM2 union. These spatial observations do not identify the executed cause or support a repair on their own.

Physical-water status remains unresolved for all ten components. The retained major-lake layer has no component intersections, but it omits complete rivers, smaller waters, and dated hydrology; official regional sources supply context rather than candidate-scale water geometry.

The source registry records both boundary products as representing 2020 and records update/build dates and license assertions. The represented year is not a legal effective date, and source metadata does not establish positional accuracy or underlying rights.
Every component remains mixed evidence with water and executed cause unresolved. No source-versus-Atlas difference proves historical processing loss, territorial ownership, or a safe geometry repair.

Official Zambia and Zimbabwe records from 2012 and 2014 describe the 1963 river-boundary definition and report interpretive/map differences and contested islands in the wider boundary region. These records support treating exact channel-side location as uncertain but do not establish that any issue component is on a disputed island or resolve the current bilateral interpretation.
